concept: A stark silhouette of a human figure standing at a crossroads or threshold, with multiple shadowy paths diverging into darkness. Behind the figure, a faint glow suggesting hope or distant light. The composition is symmetrical and monumental, rendered in bold geometric shapes with heavy pixelation in mind. The mood is contemplative but tense, with an undercurrent of uncertainty. Use muted tones transitioning from deep indigo to pale grey, suggesting dawn or dusk. Include abstract elements—cracks in the ground, fragmented architectural forms, and subtle references to barriers or bridges.
explanation: Today's headlines oscillate between tentative steps toward cooperation (Canada-EU alliance, Iran at the UN table) and brutal ruptures (murders, war crimes allegations, abductions). The overarching narrative is one of humanity at a crossroads: institutions attempting dialogue while violence, oppression, and existential risks (uncontrolled AI) escalate elsewhere. The image captures that pivot point—a figure caught between competing futures, neither wholly dark nor wholly illuminated. The pixelation and duotone treatment will reduce noise and emphasize the essential emotional geometry of indecision and fragile hope amid widespread harm.

headlines.title: Canada welcomes EU proposal to become 'associate member'
headlines.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said a Canada-EU alliance would create a "beacon for other democracies".

headlines.title: Ninth woman's body found as South African police investigate string of deaths
headlines.summary: South Africa police have cautioned against assuming that all the killings are linked but many women are afraid.

headlines.title: UN experts say grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran strikes
headlines.summary: The US has not acknowledged carrying out February's deadly strikes on a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd.

headlines.title: US to allow Iran delegation to attend UN meetings in New York as war passes half-year mark
headlines.summary: The BBC understands Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi are among the delegates allowed to enter the US.

headlines.title: Wife of US scholar jailed in China asks Trump to raise arrest at Xi meeting
headlines.summary: Sylvia Zin is among the family members of people imprisoned in China who are seeking Trump's help when he hosts the country's leader next week.

headlines.title: Hyrox athlete apologises for continuing race after soiling herself
headlines.summary: Joanna Wietrzyk has also forfeited her win in the fitness competition after competing last week.

headlines.title: Aztec document goes on display in Mexico after 186 years abroad
headlines.summary: France's national library is lending the manuscript recounting the history of the Aztecs to Mexico.

headlines.title: EU announces plan to restrict social media access for under-15s
headlines.summary: Under the plans, only children over 15 would be able to set up their own social media accounts.

headlines.title: Uncontrolled AI could lead to 'silicon species' rivalling humans, warns Microsoft
headlines.summary: Mustafa Suleyman says he believes rival AI firm Anthropic is in effect teaching Claude it "may be conscious".

headlines.title: Swedish PM Kristersson resigns after election loss
headlines.summary: Left-wing opposition parties led by Magdalena Andersson look set to form the next government.

headlines.title: Klopp wants to 'reclaim' flag amid German elections
headlines.summary: New Germany coach Jurgen Klopp says his team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right election victory.

headlines.title: Abducted South African journalist found dead with gunshot wounds
headlines.summary: The body of veteran broadcaster Owen Ndlovu was found hours after armed men kidnapped him near Johannesburg.
